# Disagreement Log — 1 Clement Chapter 27

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** 1 Clement 27
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Disagreements

**Verse 27:1 — "bound" vs. "fastened" vs. "anchored"**
- EMET: "bound"
- LOGOS: "fastened"
- PNEUMA: "anchored"
- Note: Greek *dethōsin* (to bind, tie). EMET is most literal. PNEUMA's "anchored" is evocative (cf. Heb 6:19 "anchor of the soul") but is not the Greek term. LOGOS "fastened" is a good middle path.

**Verse 27:3 — "Let faith in him be kindled again" vs. "Let faith in him be rekindled"**
- EMET: "kindled again"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA/SOPHIA: "rekindled"
- Note: Minor stylistic variation; "rekindled" is the natural English compound.

**Verse 27:3 — "all things are near to him" vs. "all things are within his reach"**
- EMET/LOGOS: "near to him"
- PNEUMA: "within his reach"
- Note: Greek *engys autō* (near to him). EMET/LOGOS is more literal; PNEUMA interprets the spatial metaphor.

**Verse 27:4 — "established" vs. "constituted" vs. "brought into existence"**
- EMET/SOPHIA: "established"
- LOGOS: "constituted"
- PNEUMA: "brought into existence"
- Note: Greek *systēsato* (established, set in order, constituted). LOGOS is precise; PNEUMA's "brought into existence" adds a creation-ex-nihilo nuance not strictly present.

**Verse 27:4 — "destroy them" vs. "overthrow them" vs. "bring them to an end" vs. "bring them to ruin"**
- EMET: "destroy them"
- LOGOS: "overthrow them"
- PNEUMA: "bring them to an end"
- SOPHIA: "bring them to ruin"
- Note: All four agents differ. Greek *katalysai* (to destroy, dissolve, overthrow). EMET "destroy" is most literal.

**Verse 27:5 — "pass away" vs. "fail"**
- EMET/LOGOS/SOPHIA: "pass away"
- PNEUMA: "fail" (adding "ever")
- Note: Greek *pareleusetai* (shall pass away). "Pass away" is standard; PNEUMA's "fail" is slightly interpretive.

**Verse 27:6 — "nothing escapes his counsel" vs. "nothing is hidden from his counsel"**
- EMET: "nothing escapes his counsel"
- LOGOS/SOPHIA: "nothing is hidden from his counsel"
- PNEUMA: "nothing escapes his notice"
- Note: Greek *panta enōpion autou estin kai ouden lelēthen tēs boulēs autou* (all things are before him and nothing has escaped his counsel). LOGOS most precisely renders the second clause.

**Verse 27:7 — "announces his handiwork" vs. "proclaims the work of his hands" vs. "announces the work of his hands"**
- EMET/SOPHIA: "announces his handiwork"
- LOGOS: "proclaims the work of his hands"
- PNEUMA: "announces the work of his hands"
- Note: Psalm 19:1 LXX. Both forms are present in manuscript traditions.

**Verse 27:7 — "Day to day utters speech" vs. "Day pours forth speech to day"**
- EMET: "Day to day utters speech"
- LOGOS/SOPHIA: "Day pours forth speech to day" / "Day after day"
- PNEUMA: "Day after day pours forth speech"
- Note: Psalm 19:2 LXX *ereugetai rhēma* (pours forth/utters a word). All three are defensible.

---

*Total disagreements: 9*
